Indian Standard PIPE THREADS WHERE PRESSURE-TIGHT JOINTS ARE NOT MADE ON THE THREADS�VERIFICATION BY MEANS OF LIMIT GAUGES
(First Revision)
NATIONAL FOREWORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) which joints are not made on the threads �Part Organization for Standardization (ISO) was recommendation of the Screw Threads Engineering Division Council. is identical with ISO 228/2:1987 `Pipe threads where pressure-tight 2: Verification by means of limit gauges', issued by the International adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 3 August 1988 on the Sectional Committee (EDC 70) and approval of the Mechanical

This standard was originally published in 1982 and was in conformity with ISO 228/2:1 980 `Pipe threads where pressure-tight joints are not made on threads� Part 2: Verification by means of limit gauges', issued by ISO, This revision of the standard has been made by the adoption of ISO 228/2:1987 to bring it in line with the latest ISO standard. In the adopted standard certain terminology and conventions Standards; attention is specially drawn to the following: are not identical with those used in Indian

a) Wherever the words `International Standard' appear referring to this standard, they should be read as `Indian Standard'. b) Comma (,) has been used as a decimal marker while in Indian Standards the current practice is to use a point (.) as the decimal marker. CROSS REFERENCES

The Technical Committee responsible for Ihe preparation of this standard has reviewed the provisions of ISO 1179: 1981 and has decided that they are acceptable for use in conjunction with this standard.
